data.description:
## Problem

`terraform apply` against `infra/terraform` **cannot complete**. The plan creates four `aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_secrets` entries, but three of them already exist in AWS and are not tracked in state:

- `/rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-claude` — exists at v1, not in state
- `/rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-codex` — exists at v1, not in state
- `/rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-copilot` — exists at v1, not in state

There is no `import` block for any of them (`grep "to = aws_ssm_parameter"` returns only the three Jira ones). The plan JSON shows `overwrite = null` on all four creates, so the provider issues `PutParameter` with `Overwrite=false` and AWS returns **`ParameterAlreadyExists`**. The apply fails partway.

`/rebar/prod/mcp-tickets-pat` does not exist, so its create is the only clean one.

Measured 2026-08-28 via `terraform plan -lock=false` plus `aws ssm describe-parameters` (metadata only — no parameter values were read).

## Impact

This blocks any `terraform apply`, which in turn blocks certified closure of `rubied-nonvagrant-whimbrel` (dd30-f10d-69f3-4c36): its AC4/DoD5 require a completed apply, and no apply can succeed until this is resolved. It is a prerequisite, not a symptom of the templatefile bug.

Live tokens are NOT at risk of being clobbered — `Overwrite=false` means the call fails rather than overwrites — so this is an availability problem, not a data-loss one.

## The fix

Add `import` blocks adopting the three parameters, mirroring the existing pattern at `ssm.tf:172-185`. `rebar_secrets` already carries `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }` (`ssm.tf:97-99`), so adoption preserves the live values rather than rewriting them.

## Operator awareness — the same plan also stops and starts live Gerrit

Separate from this bug but discovered with it, and it should be understood before ANY apply is authorised: the plan also carries `update aws_instance.gerrit` (user_data, in place). `user_data_replace_on_change` is unset so there is no replacement, but `public_ip` / `public_dns` are planned `(known after apply)` — the signature of a stop/start. That means an **outage of the Gerrit/MCP/review box and a public IP change**. The plan additionally creates two CloudWatch alarms (`mcp_mem_abort`, `mcp_retire_cap`) that are outside the templatefile fix's envelope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `import` blocks exist for all three `mcp-client-pat-*` parameters at the `rebar_secrets` addresses.
- [ ] `terraform plan` shows the three as adopted (`no-op` or in-place), NOT as `create`.
- [ ] The live parameter VALUES are unchanged after adoption — verified by version number remaining at v1, without reading the values themselves.
- [ ] A plan run reaches a state where no `ParameterAlreadyExists` failure is reachable, evidenced from the plan JSON rather than inferred.

## Testing

- Re-run `terraform plan -input=false -no-color -lock=false` and diff the `resource_changes` actions for the four parameters before and after.
- Anchor the check: confirm the plan JSON is being read for the right addresses by asserting a known-present resource appears as expected first — a query returning no `create` actions proves nothing if it is looking in the wrong place.
- Never print parameter values; assert on metadata (existence, version, action) only. Scrub any plan file afterwards, since `prior_state` can embed live SSM values.
data.title: terraform apply cannot complete: three live mcp-client-pat SSM parameters exist in AWS but are absent from state with no import block
